examples.title: Wave
examples.lesson: One gesture, standing still. The simplest thing to ask for.
examples.prompt: a person waves hello with their right hand

examples.title: Walk
examples.lesson: Travel. The character goes somewhere, and the trail shows the path.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward at a steady pace

examples.title: Jump
examples.lesson: A beat of effort: wind up, leave the ground, land.
examples.prompt: a person jumps straight up and lands

examples.title: Jab, then cross
examples.lesson: Two actions, two blocks. One action per block, each as long as it takes; the timeline sets the order.
examples.prompt: a person throws a jab → a person throws a right cross

examples.title: Run, then stop
examples.lesson: One block runs, the next stops, and two circles on one spot say where: reached by frame 100, still there at 120.
examples.prompt: a person runs forward → a person slows down and stops

examples.title: Kick the ball
examples.lesson: Pins work on feet too. The foot meets the ball at the pinned frame; move the ball and its pin together to kick somewhere else.
examples.prompt: a person kicks a ball with their right foot

examples.title: Walk and strike a pose
examples.lesson: A key pose is a keyframe the motion has to hit. This one came from Generate Pose @ Frame; make your own at any frame, or pose it by hand.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward → a person stops and raises both arms in victory

examples.title: Walk, turn, walk back
examples.lesson: A block per action sets what happens; each circle on the floor says where to be, and when. Drag one, or change its frame, and generate again.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward → a person turns around → a person walks forward

examples.title: Creep around the crate
examples.lesson: Blocks set the beats, waypoints the route, and facing along the path turns the body with it. Resize a block, or drag a circle, and generate again.
examples.prompt: a person standing upright slowly crouches down → a person creeps forward slowly in a crouch → a person stands up

examples.title: Step over the log
examples.lesson: The model does not see props; constraints tell it about them. A pin over the log for each foot, at the frame it crosses, lifts it over.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward → a person steps over a log → a person walks forward

examples.title: Aim and fire a pistol
examples.lesson: A prop in the hand is just parented to the hand bone, so it follows whatever you generate. The blocks do the rest: raise, fire, lower.
examples.prompt: a person stands still with arms relaxed at their sides → a person raises a pistol with their right hand and aims forward → a person fires a pistol twice → a person lowers both arms to their sides and relaxes

examples.title: Sword combo
examples.lesson: A combo is a block per strike. Retime a block to make a strike faster or slower, or add one.
examples.prompt: a person slashes a sword from right to left → a person slashes a sword from left to right → a person thrusts a sword forward

examples.title: Walk, then aim a rifle
examples.lesson: Two hands on one prop: the rifle rides the right hand and aims at the left, so it sits in both hands whatever you generate.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward holding a rifle → a person stops and aims a rifle → a person holds a rifle aimed forward

examples.title: Walk to the chair, sit
examples.lesson: Everything at once: a block per action, key poses for how it starts and ends, waypoints for where it walks — the last one set to face back. The seated hands were fixed with the Autoposer; try it on any key pose.
examples.prompt: a person walks forward → a person turns around → a person sits down on the chair
